sections.title: 1. What is SPOF?
sections.body:
(Architecture reliability problem)

A Single Point of Failure is a component whose failure can bring down the entire application or a critical part of it.

In simple words:

**If one component fails and the entire system stops working, that component may be a SPOF.**

sections.title: 2. Real-time GenAI example
sections.body:
Suppose your architecture uses only one LLM provider.

```text
        Users
          |
          v
     FastAPI App
          |
          v
    LLM Provider A
          |
          v
       Response
```

What happens if Provider A experiences an outage?

Your entire AI application may stop generating responses.

Even though FastAPI, PostgreSQL and Redis are healthy, the application cannot complete its main task.

sections.title: 4. Where can SPOFs exist in AI applications?
sections.body:
| Component | Possible failure |
| --- | --- |
| LLM provider | AI responses unavailable |
| API gateway | All API requests blocked |
| PostgreSQL | Application data inaccessible |
| Redis | Cache/session operations fail |
| Vector database | RAG retrieval unavailable |
| Message broker | Background jobs stop progressing |
| Agent orchestrator | Multi-agent workflow stops |
| Authentication service | Users cannot authenticate |

sections.title: 5. How to detect it?
sections.body:
Ask these questions:

- Does the application depend on only one provider?
- Is there only one application instance?
- Is there only one database instance?
- Does every agent depend on one central orchestrator?
- Is there a backup if Redis becomes unavailable?
- Are backups and recovery procedures tested?

Monitor component health, dependency availability and service-level indicators.

sections.title: 6. How to fix it?
sections.body:
- Use multiple application instances behind a load balancer.
- Configure approved LLM provider fallbacks.
- Use database replication and tested failover.
- Deploy critical infrastructure across availability zones.
- Use durable queues for asynchronous work.
- Maintain backups and disaster recovery procedures.
- Avoid unnecessary central dependencies.
- Regularly test failover.

**Important:** Redundancy does not automatically guarantee reliability. Two providers may share a common network, cloud region or authentication dependency.

**Memory trick:**

> SPOF = One component fails, and a critical part of the application becomes unavailable.

quiz.question: Single Point of Failure (SPOF): What is SPOF?
options: LLM providers restrict how frequently you can send requests and how many tokens you can process over a period.
A duplicate request occurs when the same operation is executed more than once unintentionally.
A trace ID is a unique identifier that connects events belonging to the same distributed request.
A Single Point of Failure is a component whose failure can bring down the entire application or a critical part of it.
quiz.explanation: (Architecture reliability problem) A Single Point of Failure is a component whose failure can bring down the entire application or a critical part of it. In simple words: If one component fails and the entire system stops working, that component may be a SPOF.

quiz.question: How to detect Single Point of Failure (SPOF)?
options: Error rate increases immediately after deployment; LLM response schemas change; Tool invocation failures increase.
Track: Daily token consumption; Monthly token consumption; Input/output token ratios.
Monitor: Provider deprecation announcements; Model version identifiers where available; Evaluation dataset results.
Ask these questions: Does the application depend on only one provider?; Is there only one application instance?; Is there only one database instance?.
quiz.explanation: Ask these questions: Does the application depend on only one provider? Is there only one application instance? Is there only one database instance?

quiz.question: How to fix Single Point of Failure (SPOF)?
options: In a distributed production system, budget reservations must be atomic.
Implement RBAC or ABAC; Validate permissions in the backend; Enforce tenant isolation.
Use bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter.
Use multiple application instances behind a load balancer; Configure approved LLM provider fallbacks; Use database replication and tested failover.
quiz.explanation: Use multiple application instances behind a load balancer. Configure approved LLM provider fallbacks. Use database replication and tested failover.
